slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only slot present; no mirror/backup copy observed. Game I/O loop bound (0x30 blocks x 8 bytes) only ever touches bytes 0x000-0x17F of the 512-byte EEPROM; bytes 0x180-0x1FF remain at erased fill (0xFF) in both samples and are not a second slot.

checksums.name: none_identified
checksums.formula_detail: No sum/XOR/CRC/complement routine exists in any of the 36 decompiled functions. The only integrity gate is the two-magic-word compare in FUN_08000214 (offsets 0x00 and 0x04 vs. a data constant and an unresolved indirect-call result respectively). Python verification of sum8/xor8/sum16le over the 360-byte body (offsets 0x18-0x17F) produced 0x52/0x9a/0xce98, none of which match any stored field in the file, confirming no body checksum exists anywhere else in the sample.

io_driver_functions.notes: EEPROM 8-byte block read primitive. [MMIO-SEED] in ghidra/save_related_functions.c. Serializes block address to a 1-bit stream, DMA3-sends read command+address to 0x0D000000 via FUN_08017734, DMA3-receives 68 response bits, unpacks 4x16-bit words. No static caller recorded; the game's 0x30-iteration block-read loop in FUN_08000214 behaviorally matches this function's signature but calls through an unresolved function pointer (pcRam080003cc), so the link is a HYPOTHESIS, not a confirmed call edge.

Generic DMA3 transfer trigger (source/dest/count+control via RAM-mirrored MMIO pointers, busy-polls before return). Called twice by FUN_080177b4: once to send the read command, once to receive the response. Only statically confirmed caller edge touching the save I/O stack.

High-level load entry point. Allocates/zeroes 384-byte heap buffer, device-select, 48x8-byte block read loop (unresolved pointer), two-magic-word validation, then copies out sub-fields at offsets 0x08 (1B), 0x09 (5B), 0x0E (8B), 0x18 (360B).

High-level save entry point; exact mirror of FUN_08000214. Packs sub-fields into the 384-byte buffer, stores magic word A (constant) and magic word B (result of pcRam080005d0()), then 48x8-byte block write loop with a retry/fallback call on failure.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown gameplay trigger (no static caller recorded for 0x08000214 itself in ghidra/callgraph.json). Once invoked with any param_1, zero-fills a lazily-allocated 384-byte heap buffer, reads 48 EEPROM blocks through an unresolved function pointer, validates two magic words, and memcpy's out four sub-fields.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Full static decompilation of FUN_08000214 in ghidra/decompiled.c; callgraph.json confirms calls to FUN_080001cc/FUN_080001f0 (memcpy/memset) but shows no resolved edge to the EEPROM block-read primitive, which is inferred only by loop-shape/parameter-count matching against FUN_080177b4.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unknown gameplay trigger (no static caller recorded). Mirror of the load chain: packs the in-RAM save struct into the 384-byte buffer and writes 48 EEPROM blocks through an unresolved function pointer.

caller_chains.how_mapped: Full static decompilation of FUN_080003f0; same caveat as the load chain regarding the unresolved EEPROM write-block pointer.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Invoked (hypothesized) once per EEPROM block index during the FUN_08000214 load loop.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Full static decompilation; this is the only confirmed direct call edge (0x080177b4 -> 0x08017734) in ghidra/callgraph.json that touches the save I/O stack.

fields.name: magic_word_a
fields.update_mechanism: Stored directly from global constant uRam080005c0 on save; compared against opaque data constant iRam080003d0 on load.

fields.name: magic_word_b_spbs
fields.update_mechanism: Stored from the return value of an unresolved indirect call pcRam080005d0() on save; compared against the return value of pcRam080003d4() on load.
fields.evidence: FUN_080003f0: *(undefined4*)(iVar2+4) = (*pcRam080005d0)();  FUN_08000214: piVar7[1] == (*pcRam080003d4)() gate. ASCII decode is direct byte inspection of cap-01-future-1.sav.

fields.name: header_flag_byte
fields.update_mechanism: Single-byte copy, isolated from the surrounding header fields in both load and save functions.

fields.name: header_block_8b
fields.update_mechanism: Explicit 8-byte memcpy in both directions; contains 2 bytes (offset 0x10-0x11) that stayed at erased fill (0xff) across the one observed save event.
fields.evidence: FUN_08000214: FUN_080001cc(*piVar1+0xe, uRam080003e0, 8); FUN_080003f0: FUN_080001cc(uRam080005c8, iVar2+0xe, 8); byte-diff of saves/cap-00-future-0.sav vs cap-01-future-1.sav shows offsets 0x10-0x11 unchanged.

fields.name: unused_gap_0x10
fields.update_mechanism: No writer observed to actually change this sub-span of the 8-byte copy during the one captured save event; treated as reserved/padding for this build until contradicted by further samples.
fields.evidence: Byte-by-byte diff in saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt / direct Python diff of the two .sav files: only bytes 0x10 and 0x11 inside the active 384-byte region are unchanged between the blank and populated snapshot.

fields.name: record_table
fields.update_mechanism: Explicit 360-byte (0x168) memcpy in both directions. Internally, byte-pattern analysis (not externally sourced) suggests three repeating 120-byte segments of ten 12-byte slots each, each slot holding a big-endian u32 round-number field followed by two 4-byte space-padded ASCII tag fields (observed tags: US, MD, CIR, CMS, BOB, KIM, ZEJ, MOT, NOJ, DOR, WMR, VEK, TLD, RQ, 'W R') and a descending 4-step counter sequence (0x28..0x04) marking each 120-byte segment's ten slots. This internal typing is unverified.
fields.evidence: Span size/copy calls: CONFIRMED_STATIC from FUN_08000214/FUN_080003f0. Internal field typing: pure byte-pattern inference over saves/cap-01-future-1.sav (period-120 recurrence of byte 0x28 at absolute offsets 0x25/0x9d/0x115; BE32 round-number decode of leading 4-byte words; ASCII decode of trailing tag bytes).

fields.name: unused_eeprom_tail
fields.update_mechanism: Never addressed: load/save block loops are bounded at 0x30 (48) blocks x 8 bytes = 384 bytes.
fields.evidence: Loop bounds in FUN_08000214/FUN_080003f0 (uVar6 < 0x30); both .sav files have bytes 0x180-0x1FF entirely 0xFF.

open_questions: What gameplay event(s) call FUN_08000214 (load) and FUN_080003f0 (save)? No static caller is recorded for either in ghidra/callgraph.json.
Where is the raw EEPROM write-block primitive (twin of read-side FUN_080177b4)? It is not present among the 36 decompiled functions.

What is the literal expected value of magic word A (iRam080003d0), and what does the indirect call behind magic word B (pcRam080003d4/pcRam080005d0) actually compute? Both are opaque data-segment/function-pointer references outside this extraction.

Is the 360-byte record table really three independent 120-byte segments of ten 12-byte slots, and are the leading 4-byte fields genuinely big-endian score values? This is an unverified structural hypothesis pending the fuzzing plan.
Only one populated .sav snapshot exists; a second distinct save event is needed to determine which header sub-fields (offsets 0x08, 0x09-0x0D, 0x0E-0x15) vary with game state versus staying fixed.
